structure: 伴随状语 + 分词前置
intro_zh: 还是 TomorrowX 峰会这场对谈的后半段。主持人先复述他九个月前的几句名言（「我的优势不是智商，而是敢扣扳机」），再追问：聪明人还会怎么自己绊自己、伟大的投资人和很好的投资人差在哪、他到底怎么做决定——答案是「先投资，再调查」。最后他给出三个十年预测：核聚变、太空数据中心、癌症变成可控的病。

sents.en: So last time, again about nine months ago, you said some pretty cool things.
sents.zh: 上次，大概九个月前，你说了几句挺精彩的话。

sents.en: I like that she's quoting that interview, because I've been wrong a lot in my life too.
sents.zh: 我很高兴她引的是那次采访，因为我这辈子也错过很多次。

sents.en: That was good timing.
sents.zh: 那次时机赶得好。

sents.en: Oh yeah, I'm cherry-picking for sure.
sents.zh: 那当然，我肯定是挑好的说。

sents.en: So you said, "My edge is not IQ, it's pulling the trigger."
sents.zh: 你说：「我的优势不是智商，而是敢扣扳机。」

sents.en: You said contrarianism is overrated.
sents.zh: 你说逆向投资被高估了。

sents.en: People sacrifice a lot of P&L just to be different.
sents.zh: 人们为了显得与众不同，牺牲了大量盈亏。

sents.en: And you talked about how smart people get in their own way, because they don't know when to stop doing research.
sents.zh: 你还讲到聪明人怎么自己绊自己——因为他们不知道什么时候该停止研究。

sents.en: So why don't we add one more thing to the list?
sents.zh: 那我们再往这个清单上加一条吧？

sents.en: How do smart people get in their own way?
sents.zh: 聪明人还会怎么自己绊自己？

sents.en: I'd say this business requires intellectual humility, intellectual humility that requires an open mind.
sents.zh: 我会说，这一行需要智识上的谦逊——那种需要开放心态的谦逊。

sents.en: I'm all for conviction.
sents.zh: 我完全赞成要有信念。

sents.en: I've plagiarized Mark Twain and said, "Put all your eggs in one basket, and then watch the basket very carefully."
sents.zh: 我借用过马克·吐温的话：「把所有鸡蛋放进一个篮子，然后非常仔细地盯着这个篮子。」

sents.en: Yep.
sents.zh: 对。

sents.en: So I'm good with making big concentrated bets, but sometimes people with very high IQs forget the second part: watch the basket very carefully.
sents.zh: 所以我赞成下大的集中仓位，但有时候智商很高的人会忘了后半句：非常仔细地盯着篮子。

sents.en: They're so in love with the thesis they made that they're not open-minded.
sents.zh: 他们太爱自己做出来的那套逻辑，以至于听不进别的。

hl.text: so in love with the thesis they made that they're not open-minded
hl.note: so + 形容词 + that…：太…以至于…。the thesis (that) they made 省略关系代词。

sents.en: You can have a great thesis, it can be a great bet, and things just happen, and they just don't seem to adjust as quickly as other people do.
sents.zh: 你可以有一个很好的逻辑，也可以是一笔很好的下注，但事情就是会发生，而他们就是不像别人那样能很快调整。

sents.en: So I'd say, I don't know why, but it tends to breed inflexibility.
sents.zh: 所以我会说——我也不知道为什么——聪明往往会养出僵化。

sents.en: Not always, but a lot of times.
sents.zh: 不是总这样，但很多时候是。

sents.en: And adjacent to that, you've met and mentored some incredible investors.
sents.zh: 跟这个相关的是，你见过、也带过一些了不起的投资人。

sents.en: What separates the very good ones from the great ones?
sents.zh: 很好的和伟大的，差别在哪儿？

sents.en: They've got to be unbelievably passionate about our business.
sents.zh: 他们得对我们这一行有近乎疯狂的热情。

sents.en: They've got to be intellectually curious.
sents.zh: 他们得有求知欲。

sents.en: They have to be competitive to the point of a sickness.
sents.zh: 他们得好胜到病态的地步。

sents.en: You've got to be sick.
sents.zh: 得是病态的那种。

sents.en: Like, so driven to win and so competitive, not wanting to lose.
sents.zh: 就是一心想赢、好胜心极强，死活不想输。

hl.note: 现在分词短语做伴随：前面说完 so driven… so competitive，再用 not wanting to… 补一个状态。否定直接把 not 放在 -ing 前面。

sents.en: It's not about work-life balance.
sents.zh: 这可谈不上工作和生活平衡。

sents.en: No work-life balance.
sents.zh: 没有工作生活平衡。

sents.en: But, you know, every time you buy something, there's a seller on the other side.
sents.zh: 可你想想，每次你买进什么，对面都有一个卖家。

sents.en: If you don't have an incredible work ethic, you're going to lose in our business.
sents.zh: 如果你不是特别肯下苦功，在我们这行你就会输。

sents.en: And then the fourth, and maybe the most important, is they're all disciplined.
sents.zh: 然后第四点，也许是最重要的：他们都很有纪律。

sents.en: Their disciplines may be very different, maybe different than mine, but whatever their discipline is, they stick to it.
sents.zh: 他们的纪律可能千差万别，可能和我的也不一样，但不管是什么纪律，他们都会坚持。

sents.en: And I'd say you put those four things together, that kind of answers your question, in my opinion.
sents.zh: 我觉得把这四点放在一起，就算回答了你的问题。

sents.en: So if our audience followed you around for a month, which would be weird, what would surprise them most about the way you make decisions?
sents.zh: 如果我们的听众跟着你一个月——那会有点怪——你做决定的方式最会让他们吃惊的是什么？

hl.note: which 指代前面整件事（跟着他一个月），上周的结构复习：先把事情说完，再用 which 补一句评价。

sents.en: What I call at our firm: invest, then investigate.
sents.zh: 我们公司管它叫：先投资，再调查。

sents.en: I'll hear an idea.
sents.zh: 我会听到一个点子。

sents.en: I'm a technician, too, so I'll see a chart I like.
sents.zh: 我也看技术面，所以我会看到一张喜欢的图。

sents.en: I like the story.
sents.zh: 我喜欢这个故事。

sents.en: It makes sense to me.
sents.zh: 我觉得说得通。

sents.en: Or the person who's telling me, it's in their wheelhouse, and I can see a certain passion.
sents.zh: 或者是给我讲这个点子的人——这正好是他的拿手领域，我能看出他有一股热情。

sents.en: And I'll make not a giant bet, but a big enough bet to really hurt if I'm wrong, with about 15% of the information that a traditional investor would want.
sents.zh: 然后我就下一笔不算巨大、但错了足够让我疼的仓位，手里的信息只有传统投资人想要的 15% 左右。

hl.text: with about 15% of the information that a traditional investor would want
hl.note: with + 名词短语做伴随状语：交代「在什么条件下」下注。中文的「手里只有 15% 的信息」，英文挂在句尾。

sents.en: And then give it to our research department and delve into it for two or three weeks and decide whether to add to it or get rid of it.
sents.zh: 然后交给我们的研究部门，花两三周深挖，再决定是加仓还是清掉。

sents.en: So there's a lot of betting going on, sort of a lot of intuition, with things that I probably have no business buying, but it's worked for me over time.
sents.zh: 所以这里面有很多下注的成分，也有很多直觉，买的很多东西我大概根本没资格买，但这些年下来对我是管用的。

hl.text: there's a lot of betting going on
hl.note: there's + 名词 + going on：「这里面有很多下注在进行」，描述状态的高频口语。

sents.en: So we had some pretty cool conversations bouncing through history and psychology and markets and a lot of wild hypotheticals.
sents.zh: 我们聊过一些很酷的话题，在历史、心理学和市场之间跳来跳去，还有很多天马行空的假设。

hl.text: conversations bouncing through history and psychology and markets
hl.note: 现在分词后置：conversations (that were) bouncing through…，「在历史、心理学、市场之间跳来跳去的对话」。

sents.en: I'd like to bring our audience into one of these conversations.
sents.zh: 我想把听众也拉进这样一次对话。

sents.en: Give me one or two predictions about the next 10 years that sound not that likely, but you would quietly put a 20% chance on.
sents.zh: 给我一两个关于未来十年的预测：听起来不太可能，但你心里默默给它 20% 的概率。

sents.en: I think there's a 20% chance we'll either have fusion or it'll be clear we're going to have fusion.
sents.zh: 我觉得有 20% 的可能，我们要么已经有了核聚变，要么已经能清楚看到核聚变一定会来。

sents.en: Number two, I'm in Austin, so I'd say it's at least 70%, if not higher: we're going to have data centers in space.
sents.zh: 第二，我人在奥斯汀，所以我会说至少 70%，甚至更高：我们会有太空数据中心。

sents.en: Number three, I believe... I've been on the board of Sloan Kettering for 30 years.
sents.zh: 第三，我认为……我在纪念斯隆-凯特琳癌症中心的董事会待了 30 年。

sents.en: The first 10 years, we went nowhere.
sents.zh: 头 10 年，我们毫无进展。

sents.en: But then we got genetic sequencing.
sents.zh: 后来有了基因测序。

sents.en: We figured out it was a personal disease.
sents.zh: 我们搞明白了，癌症是一种因人而异的病。

sents.en: Mutations, immunotherapy, and now AI.
sents.zh: 基因突变、免疫疗法，现在又有了 AI。

sents.en: I think we're going to beat cancer.
sents.zh: 我认为我们会战胜癌症。

sents.en: I think it's going to be a managed disease, and I mean in 10 years, not 20 years.
sents.zh: 我认为它会变成一种可控的病，我说的是 10 年内，不是 20 年。

shadow.tips: 断句：Put ALL your EGGS / in ONE BASket, / and THEN / WATCH the basket / VEry CAREfully. all your eggs 连读 al-lyour-eggs；then 后面停一下，再强调 watch。
断句：They're SO in LOVE / with the THEsis they MADE / that they're NOT / OPen-MINDed. so 拉长；thesis they 别断开。
断句：Like, / so DRIven to WIN / and so comPEtitive, / NOT WANTing to LOSE. not wanting to 连成 not-wan-ning-tə；lose 收尾重读。
断句：And I'll make NOT a GIANT bet, / but a BIG eNOUGH bet / to REALly HURT / if I'm WRONG, / with about fifTEEN PERcent / of the inforMAtion / a traDItional investor would WANT. with 前面停顿，像补充条件。
断句：So there's a LOT of BETting going ON, / sort of a lot of intuITion, / with things I probably have NO BUSiness BUYing, / but it's WORKED for me / over TIME. betting going on 一口气；no business 重读。

questions: What did Druckenmiller say last time about his edge and about contrarianism?
How do smart people get in their own way, according to him? (Try: "Being so in love with their thesis, they…")
What does the Mark Twain line mean, and which half do smart people forget?
What four traits separate the great investors from the very good ones?
Describe "invest, then investigate" step by step. (Try: "Seeing a chart he likes, he… / with only about 15% of the information…")
Which of his three 10-year predictions do you find most believable, and why?

chunks.zh: 把鸡蛋都放进一个篮子（集中下注）

chunks.zh: 错了足够让我疼的一笔仓位
